title: Count the radians per metre
hook: Change wavelength and predict angular wave number.
misconception: angular wave number doubles when wavelength doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply k = 2π/λ to compare angular wave number when wavelength changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With a sinusoidal wave, k = 2π/λ. When wavelength doubles, angular wave number becomes ½ times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model k = 2π/λ; scaling exponent -1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider a sinusoidal wave, with a nonzero initial result. If wavelength triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on angular wave number?
recall.why: Apply k = 2π/λ under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 1/3.
